citation: [1708, 1706 and 1700 S. Prairie Avenue, the homes of James and Narcissa Thorne, George and Alice Glessner, and Blewett and Frances Lee.] Photograph from the east side of Prairie Avenue, captioned 'Three of the trees from The Rocks were delivered to these Prairie Avenue homes: (L-R) James and Narcissa Thorne (1708), George and Alice Glessner (1706), and Blewett and Frances Lee (1700)'; photographer not named. Reproduced by the Glessner House Museum, 'The Glessner House Christmas Tree', The Story of a House (blog), 14 December 2021.
author: unknown photographer (probably of the Glessner family)
date: undated (after 1902; the blog's context is Christmas 1911)
repository: Glessner House Museum blog 'The Story of a House' (the museum's collection, per the blog). Prairie library image a16-ghm-blog-1708-1706-1700-christmas, its rights recorded there as 'pending - permission requested' (rights-requests/ghm-george-glessner-2026-10.md); the project's reference copy is the image store's (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a16-ghm-blog-1708-1706-1700-christmas.jpg), committed since T-3188 at data/sources/assets/thorne_1708_photos_t3188/ with its attribution.
locator: The left fifth of the photograph, x 0-190 of the 1200 px copy: 1708 Prairie's street front from its cornice to grade, the north end of it behind 1706's porch and a street lamp.
rights_note: Permission for the museum's scans was requested on 2026-10-02 and is pending; the reproduction carries no rights statement. Only forms, counts, places and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset (no texture, no traced mesh), and the copy committed for the image gate (T-3188) is the store's, unaltered, with its attribution in the folder's README.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-27 (T-3188) from the image store's reference copy, 1200 x 983 px greyscale. The Prairie library has the camera south-east of the houses looking north-west; the townhouses' cornice rises toward 1700 and 1700's north wall is in view, so it stood NORTH-east of them looking south-west (T-3188's camera).
note: The fullest picture of 1708 Prairie this project reads, at the left edge of a photograph of the Glessner townhouses. Through T-3188's camera: a flat-topped brick front of three storeys taller than the townhouses' cornice; a deep plain cornice, its soffit about 13.0 m and its top about 13.55 m over grade, over a frieze about 1.2 m deep closed below by a string course about 12.0 m up; eared hoods over the upper storeys' windows (sills about 5.7 and 9.2 m); on the south part of the front a bay rising through the lower two storeys to a flat top about 8.9 m up, the 1911 sheet's canted bay; the north end of the front behind 1706's porch; the brick north wall standing clear above 1706's cornice. It is evidence of the front after 1902.
what_it_supplies: the front's height: its cornice, frieze and string course
the upper storeys' windows, their sills, heads and eared hoods
the south bay through two storeys and its flat top
the north wall rising above 1706's cornice
what_it_does_not_supply: the ground storey's openings at the north end, hidden by 1706's porch and a street lamp
the bay's south end, the south wall, the rear and the roof
